#CyberAttack #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
A radiation alert for Kyiv. It was fake. The app was real. ☢️

What happened (The Record and Security Affairs, 2 Nov):
→ Late Sunday, Ukraine's government-backed Air Alert app sent fake radiation, chemical and street-fighting warnings, including in Kyiv
→ The app had 6.6 million active users as of January 2026
→ Ukraine's Air Force said it had "likely been compromised by the enemy" and told people to ignore the messages; a previously unknown group claimed it
→ Hours later, Russia's Ministry of Emergency Situations confirmed its own app was hacked and used to send fake nuclear launch warnings
→ Both sides said sirens, loudspeakers, texts, TV and radio kept working; the apps are supplementary

What to do: if you run any mass-notification system, limit who and what can push alerts, require two-person approval for high-severity messages, and keep an all-clear process ready.

cover.hook: No Teams bug. Just "IT support" and a certificate template.
cover.sub: Microsoft traced two intrusions from a fake help desk chat to domain controller access.

slides.title: The way in
slides.body: Attackers messaged staff on Microsoft Teams from outside tenants with support-themed names. They got users to open Quick Assist and read back the code. No Teams flaw was used.

slides.label: privileged accounts got certificates
slides.note: Case 1: two waves using an ESC1 template weakness in AD CS (Microsoft)

slides.title: One gap was enough
slides.body: Defender's automatic disruption cut off most identities. One privileged account was excluded from automatic response. It reached a file server and data was copied out to an external SFTP server.

slides.title: Case 2: ESC8
slides.body: A coerced domain controller login was relayed to the AD CS web enrollment page. The attacker got a certificate for the domain controller. Alerts fired and the workstation was isolated.

slides.title: Do this week
items: Restrict which outside Teams tenants can message staff
Audit templates where the requester picks the account
Turn on EPA and HTTPS for AD CS web enrollment
Give every containment exclusion a manual owner

items.question: Would your users read a Quick Assist code to "IT" on Teams?
items.x_text:
Microsoft Teams help desk scam + AD CS: Microsoft traced two intrusions where fake "IT support" got Quick Assist access, then abused ESC1 and ESC8 certificate weaknesses. One account excluded from auto-containment was enough to copy data out.

#ActiveDirectory #InfoSec
items.ig_caption:
No Teams bug. Just "IT support" and a certificate template. 🎫

What Microsoft found (via The Hacker News, 2 Nov):
→ Attackers messaged staff on Teams from outside tenants with support-themed names and got them to open Quick Assist
→ Case 1: an ESC1 weakness in an Active Directory Certificate Services template let low-privileged users get certificates for 11 privileged accounts across two waves
→ Defender's automatic disruption cut most of them off, but one privileged account was excluded from automatic response and was used to copy data to an external SFTP server
→ Case 2: a coerced domain controller login was relayed to AD CS web enrollment (ESC8) to get a domain controller certificate
→ Microsoft didn't tie it to any known group. The techniques date back to 2021

What to do: restrict which outside Teams tenants can contact staff, verify support requests on a known channel, audit certificate templates, enable EPA and HTTPS on AD CS web enrollment, and assign a manual action to every account excluded from auto-containment.

segments.say: Audit your M C P configs. Approve one official server per service.
segments.show: Glow found four high-severity flaws in these servers; no exploitation seen yet. Check configs for deprecated @modelcontextprotocol servers.

items.x_text:
MCPhantom: AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI) keep installing deprecated MCP servers that will never be patched, says Glow Labs. 98% of the time the name came from the model's memory. 17.3M+ npm downloads since July 2025.

#AgenticAI #AISecurity
items.ig_caption:
17 million downloads. These servers will never get a security fix. 🤖

What researchers found (Help Net Security, 3 Nov):
→ Glow Labs reviewed real AI coding sessions and named the pattern "MCPhantom"
→ In 98% of sessions where a deprecated MCP server was installed or suggested, the agent supplied the package name from its training data
→ Seen across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI and others, with models from Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI
→ The deprecated packages have 17.3 million+ npm downloads since July 2025; they're archived, so no patches are coming
→ Glow found four high-severity flaws in them, the worst a remote code execution in the Puppeteer server. No exploitation seen yet
→ They don't show up in dependency files, so SCA tools miss them

What to do: search MCP configs for deprecated @modelcontextprotocol servers, switch to the service owner's official server, approve one server per service, and treat the agent's package choices as untrusted.

cover.hook: $46M+ left Latin America's biggest crypto platform overnight.
cover.sub: Mercado Bitcoin froze deposits and withdrawals. Experts dispute its "no customer harm" line.

slides.title: What happened
slides.body: Brazil's Mercado Bitcoin suspended all deposits and withdrawals after a cybersecurity incident on Monday morning. Blockchain security firms say the money started moving late Sunday night.

slides.label: left the platform, per blockchain security firms
slides.note: Mercado Bitcoin has not confirmed the figure (The Record)

slides.title: The dispute
slides.body: Mercado says customers weren't harmed and there was no data breach. Several blockchain security experts disagree, pointing to on-chain evidence that funds were taken from some customer wallets.

slides.title: Clawing it back
slides.body: Tether's CEO says about $4.5M was frozen; other platforms froze about $2M more. Mercado shared the destination addresses and says it will restore service "in the coming days". It has about 4.5 million customers.

slides.title: Do this week
items: Exchange user? Don't send funds until it's officially back
Ignore "refund" DMs: scammers follow every heist
Keep long-term holdings in a wallet you control
Exchanges: alert on hot-wallet outflow spikes

Mercado Bitcoin hack: Brazil's largest crypto platform froze deposits and withdrawals after blockchain firms saw $46M+ flow out late Sunday. Mercado says no customer harm; experts dispute it. About $6.5M frozen so far.

#CryptoHack #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
$46M+ left Latin America's biggest crypto platform overnight. 🪙

What we know (The Record, 2 Nov):
→ Brazil's Mercado Bitcoin suspended all deposits and withdrawals after a cybersecurity incident on Monday morning
→ Blockchain security firms say more than $46 million left the platform late Sunday night; Mercado hasn't confirmed the figure
→ Mercado says customers weren't harmed and there was no data breach. Several blockchain experts dispute that, citing on-chain evidence from customer wallets
→ Tether's CEO says about $4.5M was frozen; other platforms froze about $2M more
→ Mercado says it has about 4.5 million customers and will restore service "in the coming days"
→ It comes days after the $6.3B Binance theft

What to do: if you use Mercado Bitcoin, wait for official word before moving funds and ignore "refund" messages. Keep long-term holdings in a wallet you control.

#PatchNow #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
One web request. No login. A bot downloaded and running. ⚙️

What VulnCheck saw (2 Nov):
→ On 30 Oct, one request to the Node-RED admin API deployed a flow that downloaded and ran a Linux binary on a VulnCheck canary
→ The flaw, CVE-2026-58115, gives unauthenticated access to nodes that can run system commands; the CVE names Siemens' SIMATIC IoT2050 Advance industrial gateway
→ 16 events against it from one IP between 30 Oct and 1 Nov, later with webshells
→ VulnCheck: "Node-RED instances without adminAuth are being found and exploited automatically"
→ Not in CISA's KEV yet; VulnCheck added it to its own

What to do: enable adminAuth, take the Node-RED editor off the internet, check Siemens' advisory for fixes, and review flows for exec nodes or HTTP endpoints you didn't build.
